paper_metadata.title: A novel approach for quantum financial simulation and quantum state preparation

summary: The paper introduces a variational multi‑Split‑Step Quantum Walk (multi‑SSQW) circuit for quantum state preparation and financial distribution modeling. Simulator experiments fit 16‑bin stock return distributions (e.g., JNJ, S&P500, Nasdaq100) using 1–10 walkers and approximate binomial distributions (n=31, 63, 127) and a log‑normal distribution for European call option pricing, yielding an expected payoff of 0.1460 compared to the analytic value 0.1739. All results are obtained on an IBM Q Experience simulator with hybrid COBYLA optimization and no demonstrated quantum speedup.

experiments.description: Multi-Split-Steps Quantum Walk (multi-SSQW) used as a variational quantum circuit to fit real stock daily-return distributions (e.g., JNJ, S&P500, Nasdaq100, Apple, Microsoft) with a classical COBYLA optimizer.

algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized quantum circuit based on multi-SSQW; U3 gates for initial state and coin operations, plus shift operators S+ and S-
algorithm.convergence_criteria: iterate until convergence to target distribution
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random parameters used in optimization simulations; initial state set by U3 gate

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one ancilla/coin qubit controls position-space evolution; N position qubits represent 2^N distribution bins
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize discrepancy between trained and target probability distributions using MSE and KL divergence

problem_instance.description: Fit empirical daily-return histograms of financial assets/indices using multi-SSQW
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: collect daily stock data from Yahoo Finance; compute daily returns; categorize into 16 distinct groups based on return percentages; convert to frequency distribution histogram
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 simulation runs for each configuration; vary number of walkers from 1 to 10; report error progression, boxplots, and average computational time

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: empirical stock data fetched from Yahoo Finance; returns binned into 16 categories
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute MSE and KL divergence; generate boxplots and average runtime
